The HENCKELS Kitchen Shears (around $15) take the opposite approach — no-nonsense German engineering, forged stainless steel, and decades of cutlery expertise.

Can whimsy compete with tradition? We put them both through a battery of kitchen tests to find out.

First Impressions

Unboxing these two could not be more different. The Elizabat arrives in OTOTO's characteristically playful packaging — it's clearly designed to be a gift or a statement piece. The bat-wing handles immediately catch your eye, and at just 3.2 ounces, it feels almost toy-like. That's not a knock — it's a design choice. OTOTO makes kitchen tools that are fun first, functional second.

The HENCKELS Kitchen Shears come in straightforward packaging. Pick them up and you immediately feel the difference — these are tools. The forged stainless steel blades have a satisfying heft, and the soft-grip handle inserts promise control even with wet or greasy hands. These were designed by people who think about cutting all day.

Right out of the gate, it's clear these scissors serve different masters. But which one should end up in your kitchen?

Cutting Performance

We tested both scissors on a series of common kitchen tasks: fresh herbs (parsley and chives), raw chicken breast, trimmed green beans, opened plastic clamshell packaging, and kitchen twine.

Herbs & Vegetables

Both scissors handled fresh herbs well, but the HENCKELS had noticeably cleaner cuts through parsley stems. The Elizabat's blades are sharp — genuinely sharp — but the lighter weight means you need to apply more downward force. For chives and soft herbs, both were perfectly adequate. The Elizabat actually felt more nimble for quick snips thanks to its low weight.

Edge: HENCKELS for cleaner cuts, Elizabat for speed on small jobs.

Poultry & Heavy Duty

This is where the gap widens into a canyon. The HENCKELS shears cleanly snipped through raw chicken skin and cartilage without slipping. The serrated edge on one blade grabs what you're cutting, and the soft-grip handles stayed secure even with slightly greasy hands.

The Elizabat struggled here. The bat-wing handles are cute, but they don't offer the same mechanical advantage for tougher cuts. We wouldn't recommend them for breaking down a whole chicken or cutting through thick meat. They're simply not designed for it.

Winner: HENCKELS — by a wide margin.

Packaging & Light Duty

For opening clamshell plastic packaging, snipping kitchen twine, cutting parchment paper, and trimming pizza — both performed well. The Elizabat's pointed tips are actually better for piercing through plastic packaging film. And the bat design makes them easy to spot in a cluttered drawer (which is genuinely useful).

Winner: Tie — different strengths, same result.

Ergonomics & Comfort

Let's be honest: the Elizabat's bat-wing handles look awesome, but they're not winning any ergonomics awards. The plastic wing shape forces your fingers into a specific position that works fine for short tasks but gets uncomfortable during extended use. The circular finger holes are on the smaller side — if you have larger hands, they may feel cramped.

The HENCKELS shears have a more conventional design with oversized soft-grip handles that accommodate all hand sizes. The asymmetrical handle design (larger thumb loop, offset finger loop) follows natural hand anatomy, reducing fatigue during prolonged cutting sessions. The rubberized inserts prevent slipping even with wet hands.

Winner: HENCKELS — significantly better for extended use.

Build Quality & Durability

HENCKELS has been making cutlery since 1731 — nearly 300 years of blade expertise. Their kitchen shears are forged from high-carbon German stainless steel that's been ice-hardened for edge retention. The blades come apart for thorough cleaning (a key feature for food-safe shears), and they carry a lifetime warranty. These are buy-it-for-life tools.

The Elizabat scissors are well-made for their price point — the stainless steel blades are adequate, and the plastic handles are securely attached. But they're not designed to last decades. The plastic bat wings could crack if dropped, and the blades will dull faster than forged steel with heavy use. For $9.99, that's acceptable — they're meant to be fun, not heirlooms.

Winner: HENCKELS — there's no substitute for forged steel and a lifetime warranty.

Cleaning & Maintenance

Both scissors are dishwasher safe, though hand washing is recommended for both to preserve blade sharpness. The HENCKELS pull-apart design (a simple screw mechanism separates the blades) makes it easy to clean between the blades — critical when you're cutting raw chicken.

The Elizabat's bat-wing handles make it harder to clean thoroughly around the pivot point. The crevices where the plastic wings meet the blade assembly can trap food particles. It's not a dealbreaker, but it requires more attention during cleaning.

Winner: HENCKELS — the take-apart design is a clear advantage for food safety.

The "Fun Factor" — Don't Underestimate It

Here's where the Elizabat makes its case. Cooking should be enjoyable, and there's genuine joy in pulling out a pair of bat-wing scissors when you're prepping dinner. OTOTO's design philosophy is that kitchen tools shouldn't be boring — and they're right. The Elizabat makes a fantastic gift for Halloween lovers, goth aesthetics, or anyone who appreciates whimsy in their kitchen.

The HENCKELS shears are the adult-in-the-room choice. They're serious, professional, and utterly lacking in personality. They'll never make you smile when you pull them out of the drawer — but they'll also never let you down.

Winner: Elizabat — for the moments when cooking should be fun.

Price & Value

The Elizabat is just $9.99 — an impulse-buy price for a unique kitchen tool. If you need a pair of scissors for light kitchen tasks and want something that sparks joy, it's an easy decision.

The HENCKELS shears cost around $14.99 (often on sale from $19.99). That's $5 more for dramatically better build quality, a lifetime warranty, and performance that will last for years. For anyone who cooks regularly, that $5 is the best investment you'll make in your kitchen toolkit.

Winner: HENCKELS — the value per year of use is unmatched when you factor in durability.

🏆 Our Pick: Elizabat Kitchen Scissors

Wait — we picked the Elizabat? Yes, and here's why.

For the typical home cook — someone who needs kitchen scissors for snipping herbs, opening packages, trimming green beans, and the occasional pizza slice — the Elizabat delivers everything you need at half the price of most competitors. It's sharp enough for daily tasks, lightweight and nimble, and it brings a smile to your face every time you use it.

But this pick comes with a caveat: the HENCKELS are objectively the better tool.

If you're a serious home cook who breaks down whole chickens, cuts through cartilage, or uses kitchen shears multiple times a day — get the HENCKELS. The forged German steel, lifetime warranty, superior ergonomics, and poultry-ready performance make them the clear choice for heavy users.

But for the majority of people — those who want a capable, affordable, and genuinely fun pair of kitchen scissors — the Elizabat is our pick. It's the kind of tool that makes cooking more enjoyable, and at $9.99, there's no reason not to try it.

Pro tip: Get both. Use the Elizabat for everyday light duty and keep the HENCKELS for heavy jobs. Your kitchen will thank you.
